key_insight: Point2Part reframes 3D part decomposition as a full-shape partitioning problem: predicted parts should be non-overlapping and together reconstruct the entire object. This makes part prediction more consistent and useful for downstream 3D tasks.
problem_solved: Most existing 3D part decomposition methods can produce overlapping parts or leave gaps, so the parts do not form a complete, clean partition of the original shape. This limits reliability for part-level editing, analysis, and other downstream applications.
method: Uses point prompts to guide the decomposition of a 3D shape into parts.
Predicts all desired parts jointly, rather than one part at a time, to enforce consistency across the whole object.
Formulates the output as a unified partition so parts are non-overlapping and collectively cover the entire shape.
impact: This approach improves the structural validity of 3D part decomposition, making the results easier to use in robotics, CAD, asset editing, and other part-aware workflows. For practitioners, it offers cleaner and more dependable part annotations/predictions for downstream pipelines.
visual_elements: A 3D object split into colored, non-overlapping parts
A side-by-side comparison of overlapping/gappy parts vs. unified partitioning
An input-output pipeline showing point prompts leading to full-shape part prediction
A coverage diagram illustrating complete reconstruction with no gaps or overlaps
paper_title: Point2Part: Unified 3D Partitioning from Point Prompts
paper_authors: Hao-Tang Tsui, Yu-Rou Tuan, Xiaoxuan Ma, Nicolas Ugrinovic, Takaaki Shiratori
